assessment: One must appreciate the challenges of antimicrobial stewardship in an immunocompromised population. This retrospective single-institution study provides valuable support for the working hypothesis that initial procalcitonin levels might be used in cancer patients admitted with COVID-19 infection to omit, reduce, or de-escalate the need for empiric antimicrobial therapy. In the setting of a global pandemic, this is a common issue with COVID-19 patients in general, but far more difficult in a cancer patient population. The results presented are solid, however, future subgroup analysis of more specific scenarios among cancer patients with COVID-19 (e.g., neutropenia, active chemotherapy, and need for intensive care) are warranted.
